_meta.description: Bundled PrusaSlicer/OrcaSlicer settings keyed by printer_id. Each profile contains INI-style key-value pairs that can be written to a temporary .ini file and passed to the slicer via --load. Also includes multi-material add-on definitions under _multi_material_addons.

_multi_material_addons._description: Optional multi-material add-on systems that can be attached to printers without built-in tool changers. Each add-on overrides the printer's default tool_change data when specified via tool_changer_addon parameter.

warnings: CFS-C slot control is hardware-unverified in Kiln; verify slot mapping on real hardware before unattended multicolor printing.
Stock K1-series printers are single-material until the CFS-C hardware, firmware update, and compatible hotend path are installed.
creality_cfs.notes: Creality CFS-C retrofit for K1/K1 Max/K1C/K1 SE. One four-slot CFS-C unit; multiple CFS-C units are not supported. Requires CFS-C hardware, firmware update, and compatible quick-swap/integrated-nozzle hotend path. Source: Creality CFS-C product specs and K1 Series Multicolor Upgrade notes (2026).

mosaic_palette3.notes: Pre-splicing system — filament is joined upstream before reaching the nozzle, so actual print pause is near-zero. 28s is the splice time; purge tower extrusion adds wall-clock time at print speed. Works with virtually any single-extruder FDM printer. Source: Mosaic product specs + splice tuning documentation.

coprint_kcm.notes: Klipper Chroma Module — 4s mechanical swap via 8-in-1 hub, plus ~26s purge. Compatible with any Klipper printer (Neptune 4, Voron, Sovol SV08, etc). Requires hardware install + custom Klipper macros. Source: Co Print product page + community benchmarks.

chameleon_mk4.notes: Open-source universal multi-material system. Button-pulse timing at ~1 inch/sec filament movement. 30-35s mechanical swap + purge. Slowest add-on but cheapest and most universal. Up to 4 colors. Source: 3D Chameleon FAQ + GitHub Mk4 documentation.

elegoo_canvas.notes: Integrated multi-color system for Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo. Not a retrofit add-on — built into the CC2 Combo variant. 70s average per color change. RFID filament detection. Source: NotebookCheck CC2 review (Jan 2026).

default.notes: Conservative defaults for unknown printers. 0.2mm layer height, 20% infill, moderate speeds.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: Generic default — manual M600 pause assumed

tool_change.tool_change_notes: Prusa MMU2S: PrusaSlicer bundled profiles use 15s load + 12s unload = 27s mechanical + ~48s purge. Capped at MMU3 FW 3.0.3 (no speed boost). High variance. Source: PrusaSlicer PrusaResearch.ini.

prusa_mk4.notes: Nextruder — low retraction distance. Input shaping enabled. PrusaSlicer 2.7+ recommended.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: Prusa MMU3: 42s mechanical (FW 3.0.4, 20% speedup from 52s) + ~23s purge. Source: Prusa blog 2025, FW 6.5.3 + MMU3 FW 3.0.4.

prusa_mini.notes: Bowden PTFE. Longer retraction than MK3S. Small build volume.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: Prusa Mini is NOT compatible with MMU2S or MMU3. Official Prusa MMU targets MK3.9/MK4 only. M600 manual pause only. Source: Prusa MMU3 compatibility page.

bambu_x1c.notes: Enclosed CoreXY. Hardened nozzle. High speeds. CRITICAL: All Bambu printers require use_relative_e_distances (M83) and empty start/end gcode — Kiln's bambu_3mf module injects BambuStudio's proprietary init sequence. Without these, extrusion silently fails.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: Bambu AMS: 28s unload + 29s load = 57s mechanical + ~40s purge (default 400mm³). Source: BambuStudio fdm_machine_common.json + X1C 0.4 nozzle.json.

bambu_x1e.notes: Enclosed CoreXY, enterprise variant. Factory hardened-steel nozzle. Active heated chamber (40-60C). 320C hotend ceiling vs 300C on the X1C. CRITICAL: All Bambu printers require use_relative_e_distances (M83) and empty start/end gcode; Kiln's bambu_3mf module injects BambuStudio's proprietary init sequence. Without these, extrusion silently fails.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: Bambu AMS: 28s unload + 29s load = 57s mechanical + ~40s purge (default 400mm³). Source: BambuStudio fdm_machine_common.json + X1C 0.4 nozzle.json.

bambu_p1s.notes: Enclosed CoreXY. Same toolhead as X1C without LiDAR. CRITICAL: All Bambu printers require use_relative_e_distances (M83) and empty start/end gcode — Kiln's bambu_3mf module injects BambuStudio's proprietary init sequence.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: Bambu AMS: 28s unload + 29s load = 57s mechanical + ~40s purge. Same AMS as X1C. Source: BambuStudio P1S 0.4 nozzle.json.

bambu_p2s.notes: Enclosed CoreXY, PMSM servo direct drive. Factory hardened-steel nozzle (abrasive-ready). AMS 2 Pro multi-material. 600 mm/s toolhead. CRITICAL: All Bambu printers require use_relative_e_distances (M83) and empty start/end gcode; Kiln's bambu_3mf module injects BambuStudio's proprietary init sequence.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: AMS 2 Pro: same mechanical tool-change envelope as the X1C/P1S AMS (28s unload + 29s load + ~40s purge). Multi-unit + active-dryer addressing is a separate adapter follow-on.

bambu_a1.notes: Open-frame bed-slinger. All-metal hotend. CRITICAL: Bambu A1 requires use_relative_e_distances (M83) for the T1000 virtual tool. Start/end gcode MUST be empty — Kiln's bambu_3mf module injects BambuStudio's proprietary 620-line init sequence (M620 M motor enable, AMS load, extrusion calibration, bed leveling) and end sequence (AMS retract, cooldown, finish sound). Without these, G1 E commands are silently ignored. Speeds proven on A1 Combo firmware 01.08.03.00.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: Bambu AMS Lite: 29s unload + 25s load = 54s mechanical + ~40s purge. Shorter PTFE path than AMS. Source: BambuStudio A1 0.4 nozzle.json.

bambu_a2l.notes: Open-frame large-format bed-slinger (330x320x325). PMSM servo extruder; stainless nozzle (fit hardened for CF). CRITICAL: like every Bambu, requires use_relative_e_distances (M83) and EMPTY start/end gcode - Kiln's bambu_3mf module injects BambuStudio's proprietary init/end sequence; without it G1 E moves are silently ignored. Field-proven on real A2L hardware; BambuStudio now ships the dedicated A2L machine profile (its own init/end gcode), which bambu_3mf injects.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: A2L Combo ships the AMS Lite (29s unload + 25s load = 54s mechanical + ~40s purge), mirrored from the A1. The A2L also supports box-style AMS / AMS 2 Pro via the AMS Hub (up to 19 colours) - see the kiln-pro AMS intelligence overlay. NOT A2L-measured.

bambu_h2s.notes: Enclosed CoreXY, direct drive. Factory hardened-steel nozzle (abrasive-ready). Active heated chamber (to 65C), 120C bed, 350C hotend - full engineering-material range. AMS 2 Pro multi-material. 1000 mm/s toolhead. CRITICAL: All Bambu printers require use_relative_e_distances (M83) and empty start/end gcode; Kiln's bambu_3mf module injects BambuStudio's proprietary init sequence. NOT YET hardware-proven on the H2S (mirrors the enclosed P2S/X1 kinematic class); verify the H2S BambuStudio machine init before relying on it.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: AMS 2 Pro: same mechanical tool-change envelope as the X1C/P1S AMS (28s unload + 29s load + ~40s purge). Multi-unit + active-dryer addressing is a separate adapter follow-on. NOT H2S-measured.

aon_m2_plus.notes: Industrial high-temperature FFF. Dual independent extruders, actively heated 135 C chamber, 500 C+ extruder, 200 C+ bed. AON3D ships a Klipper-based firmware on current machines (units at or below application version v2022.07.04.21.14 run Marlin) behind AON3D's own browser interface. They document no Moonraker port or third-party control endpoint, so Kiln does not claim a control path to it — the intelligence here is advisory until a machine is tested.

ender3_s1_pro.notes: Sprite Pro full-metal direct-drive extruder — rated to 300C with a titanium throat and no PTFE in the hot zone, so high-temperature filaments are safe here in a way they are not on the base S1. Open-frame bed-slinger, so ABS and ASA still warp without an enclosure.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: No automatic tool changer. M600 manual pause only.

aon_hylo.notes: AON3D recommends SuperSlicer and ships validated material profiles with the machine — prefer those over this generic profile, which exists to give correct envelope and nozzle limits. SuperSlicer is a PrusaSlicer derivative. 0.6 mm is AON3D's stated standard nozzle; 0.2-1.2 mm are offered.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: Dual independent extruders: the second tool is a real toolhead, not a filament swap, so support material runs at its own temperature. No manual pause needed.

intamsys_610ht.notes: SET THE NOZZLE DIAMETER BEFORE SLICING. INTAMSYS publishes none for this model and the machine takes it from the operator, so the 0.4 mm here is a placeholder, not a spec — slicing against the wrong one gives you silently wrong extrusion widths. Filament is 1.75 mm or 2.85 mm depending on configuration; confirm yours too. INTAMSYS ships INTAMSUITE NEO and the machine accepts gcode over USB or FTP; this generic profile exists to give correct envelope limits.

tool_change.tool_change_notes: Two nozzles on one print head; soluble and breakaway support materials are supported. No automatic tool changer beyond the second nozzle.

visionminer_22idex_v4.notes: Vision Miner publishes 'Standard G-code, RepRap based' and names PrusaSlicer, Simplify3D, Slic3r and OrcaSlicer as compatible, so this profile slices for the real machine rather than approximating it. 0.4 mm hardened steel is the included nozzle (E3D v6 style M6x1).

tool_change.tool_change_notes: True IDEX: two independent carriages, so a support or second material runs at its own temperature. No manual pause needed.
